craft_claim: Non-Anglophone oral comic traditions (Japanese rakugo, Chinese xiangsheng) carry humour through performed timing, character voice, and patterned sound, not only verbal content.

supporting_evidence.location: Chapters on Kamigata rakugo history and technique
supporting_evidence.note: Rakugo is a centuries-old solo comic-storytelling form in which a seated performer voices all characters and builds humour through pacing, character voice, and patterned repetition.

supporting_evidence.location: Analysis of hidden musicality in xiangsheng
supporting_evidence.note: Shows that Chinese xiangsheng speech carries patterned rhythm and sound features that are central to its comic effect, so verbal comedy is also sonic and sequential.

counterevidence.note: Section E transfer limit: the performance features (pause, vocal contrast) cannot be fully transferred to prose modelling from a monograph, so timing and character voice are documented as cross-cultural levers in performance rather than as recoverable prose operators.

scope: Cross-cultural validity of comic craft levers; performance traditions as evidence that timing and voice are not Anglophone inventions.
exceptions: Performance features (pause, vocal contrast) are not fully transferable to prose modelling.
Translation mediation limits claims about original-language wordplay and prosody.
